reason: The specified independent-sign, alternating-mean model agrees with the canonical witness after changing from one-based to zero-based indices. T11 states all scaling/validity/homoskedasticity assertions, the finite decomposition and remainder moments, the even-size mean-square formula and both lower bounds, the V2star=V2 identities, convergence of the scaled difference to 1, both failure-event limits (indeed for all sizes rather than just an even subsequence), and one-sided conservativeness (for every positive epsilon). The row laws are the restrictions of one infinite independent-sign sequence, so their presentation as marginal laws loses no raw-outcome nesting condition. Finite support excludes undefined moments and the common variance t_n^2 is positive. The witness satisfies every condition of the printed proof-step reading as well as its intended consistency reading.

T12WholeStatement includes each assertion of canonical clauses (i)-(iv), identifies the common weighted variance, and states the final one-sided probability limit. WholeScaling imposes the rowwise boundedness, dependency, degree, coefficient and variance-limit conditions of Assumption 2 without requiring nested observed graphs. This covers nested full graphs with changing observed sets and in fact proves the same rowwise conclusion for arbitrary observed arrays. There is no equal-means, positive-row-variance, mean-spread-limit, variance-limit-for-individual-units, auxiliary-correlation, or Proposition-1 hypothesis. The nested alternating-sign family supplies all hypotheses with constants (2,1,1,2). The certified-bound setting implies existence of all weighted moments; no junk-value convention is used.

The statement retains the finite feasible-set test, existential forced/optional decomposition, optimal decoding and exact weight recovery for every supplied maximum matching, exact gadget cardinalities and polynomial combinatorial size bounds, and both attained four-vertex instances. It does not explicitly state canonical (a)'s equivalences with the paper's programs, (b)'s uniqueness and separate optional optimum identity, general maximum-matching existence or an independently defined optimum-value equation in (c), or (e)'s algorithmic runtime and complexity-class consequences. These are exactly the omissions already identified in the Challenge docstring. Natural truncated residual capacities are used correctly: the feasibility test uses unsaturated inequalities and decoding is guarded by feasibility. The rational denominator LCM is positive even with no optional edges. Exhaustive rational enumeration confirms both specified graph and gadget optima, and finite maximization gives genuine maximum matchings.

RelaxedFeasible is exactly the box, forced-edge and incidence-degree LP relaxation. The general statement applies any certified global LP upper bound to every integer feasible point and both variance formulas, hence includes the optimized LP value and integer maximizers in canonical (a). Naming independent optimum constants or an optimizer is unnecessary to this universal inequality. The six-unit and triangle clauses include fractional feasibility, exact attained values, global LP and integer bounds, the ordered-pair factors of two and both six-unit variance values. The named integer witness is the canonical two-edge graph. The additional existence of a worse relaxed-feasible point is the claimed failure of arbitrary feasible objective values as upper bounds. Positive sizes exclude zero denominators. Independent enumeration verifies the integer optima and fractional feasibility; the global fractional bounds follow by summing the capacity constraints.
